name: Punic

ancestors.notes: Punic is a Late/Western dialect continuation of Phoenician, spoken at Carthage and other western Mediterranean colonies from ~8th c. BCE to ~6th c. CE.

Wikipedia (Punic language): from the 2nd century BCE, and especially after the fall of Carthage (146 BCE), Punic underwent phonological/morphological changes 'probably influenced by the language of the Berbers'; this Late/Neo-Punic layer survived among North African peasants into the 6th century CE.

notes: STUB. Punic (Phoenicio-Punic), an extinct offshoot of Phoenician spoken on the Mediterranean coast of Northwest Africa (Carthage), the Iberian Peninsula and Mediterranean islands (Malta, Sicily, Sardinia), 8th c. BCE - 6th c. CE. Written in the Punic alphabet (monumental) and the cursive Neo-Punic alphabet, both descended from the Phoenician abjad; this repo does not model the native script (orthography_kind is left as a placeholder for scholarly Latin transliteration, not yet populated). Krahmalkov (2001) reconstructs 22 consonants from Latin/Greek transcriptions (e.g. the 'Poenulus' passages in Plautus); known sound changes from Phoenician include: b > v and p > f (fricativisation, attested from the 3rd c. BCE), loss of glottal stop and pharyngeal/laryngeal consonants in Late Punic and Neo-Punic, word-final g > ɣ and k > x (spirantisation), and merger of the four Phoenician sibilants s/š/ṣ/z toward /s/ in Late Punic. No grapheme table is populated here: unlike phn.json (whose vowel-augmented Latin transliteration convention and consonant values are well established via comparison with Hebrew/Greek transcriptions), a citable, complete letter-to-IPA table specific to Punic (as opposed to Phoenician proper) was not sourced this session with confidence sufficient to assert one; adding it is future work. This spec exists so xpu resolves as a leaf under phn per the design rule against dangling ancestry references. Never fabricate a Latin-placeholder inventory: graphemes is intentionally empty pending a sourced transliteration table.
